tracker.title: Tracker
tracker.subtitle: Follow every application in one list. Drafts go to Gmail; you always send them yourself.
tracker.helpBody0: Each row is one job application. CMAE reads your related Gmail and updates the status as the conversation changes — you do not set statuses by hand.
tracker.helpBody1: Days mentioned below (when to follow up, when something closes) can be changed in Settings.
tracker.status0Text: Research finished; nothing sent yet. Status shows Research done until you create a Gmail draft, then Mail in draft while it waits in Gmail Drafts for you to send.
tracker.status1Text: The company wrote something that needs your answer — for example a question, interview invite, or offer.
tracker.status2Text: They asked you to open a link, fill a form, or complete a test — not only write a normal reply.
tracker.status3Text: You have waited long enough with no real reply. A gentle nudge makes sense now.
tracker.status4Text: There is a known date ahead — for example an interview day, or when someone said they are back from leave.
tracker.status5Text: The ball is with them for now. It is not yet time to follow up, and nothing urgent is waiting on you.
tracker.status6Text: They said no. A short thank-you is often nice; if you stay silent for a while, the row closes on its own.
tracker.status7Text: This application is finished — you withdrew, you thanked them after a rejection, or nobody replied for a long time.
tracker.status8Text: You paused this row yourself. CMAE stops treating it as something to act on until you turn it back on.
tracker.status9Text: Set aside — not part of your active follow-up list.
tracker.helpStep0: Run Gmail sync to load recent mail. Turn on Thorough sync if something looks missing (last ~30 days).
tracker.helpStep1: Companies from Research also appear here automatically.
tracker.helpStep2: For a follow-up, reply, or thank-you, use the action — CMAE writes a draft into Gmail Drafts.
tracker.helpStep3: Click a company row to open its timeline. You always send from Gmail yourself; CMAE never sends mail for you.

faq.sendQ: Does CMAE send emails for me?
faq.sendA: No. CMAE never sends mail. It writes into Gmail Drafts (with your CV attached when relevant). You open Gmail, review, and send yourself.
faq.freeA: The desktop app itself is free. You bring a Gmail App Password and a Cursor API key; you pay Cursor for API usage on your own account.
faq.needQ: What do I need to get started?
faq.needA: Three things: a Gmail account with a Google App Password (2-Step Verification), a Cursor API key (powers Research and email drafting), and at least one CV as PDF. Keys stay encrypted on your machine; you can add more CVs (languages/labels) later in Settings.
faq.privacyQ: Where is my data stored? Is it private?
faq.privacyA: Workspace data lives on your computer (SQLite + userData): company folders, CVs, Tracker state, and settings. Your Gmail App Password and Cursor API key are encrypted locally and are never uploaded to CMAE servers. Research and draft generation send content to your Cursor account via the API key. Separately, choosing a non-English UI language may use an optional remote step to build a language pack.
faq.gmailQ: Why Gmail only — and what is an App Password?
faq.gmailA: CMAE syncs mail and saves drafts via Gmail IMAP with a Google App Password — not your normal Gmail password. Outlook and other providers are not supported yet. The App Password is encrypted and stored only on your computer.
faq.platformsA: macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) via .dmg, and Windows x64 via .exe. Intel Macs and Linux are not offered yet. There is no browser app — day-to-day use is the desktop client so credentials and research files stay local.
faq.osWarnQ: Why does my OS warn when I install or open CMAE?
faq.osWarnA: On Mac, first launch after download: right-click CMAE → Open → confirm (Gatekeeper). On Windows, unsigned builds often hit SmartScreen — choose More info → Run anyway. Signed builds reduce these warnings.
faq.whatA: CMAE (Cold Mail AI Engine) is a local-first desktop app for job outreach that never sends mail for you. You get Research, Folders, Tracker, and Settings in one place.
faq.onlineQ: Do I need to be online?
faq.onlineA: Yes for Research (fetching pages + Cursor), Gmail sync, and updates. Browsing already-saved Folders and reviewing Tracker rows works offline once data is on disk.
faq.updatesA: The app checks for a newer build and can prompt you to download it. Installing a newer .dmg or .exe keeps your userData. Do not use Settings → wipe if you only meant to upgrade.
faq.langQ: Can I change the interface language?
faq.langA: Yes, in onboarding or Settings. UI language packs can be generated for your locale. Emails to companies still follow each company’s language; translated copies are for you.
faq.wipeA: Settings includes a full wipe of local settings, mail cache, tracker, CVs, company folders, and research history on this computer. It cannot be undone — you will set up CMAE again from scratch.
